policy_name: New York City Local Law 144 of 2021 on Automated Employment Decision Tools (NYC Admin. Code §§ 20-870 to 20-874) and DCWP implementing rules (6 RCNY §§ 5-300 to 5-304)
issuing_authority: New York City Council; implemented and enforced by the NYC Department of Consumer and Worker Protection (DCWP)
country_region: New York City, New York, United States
regulatory_regime: NYC Administrative Code Title 20, Chapter 5, Subchapter 25 (Automated Employment Decision Tools)
geo_constraints: Employers and employment agencies using AEDTs for candidates for employment or employees for promotion who reside in New York City (DCWP rules tie applicability to NYC-located jobs/offices)

key_dates.event: Law takes effect (enforcement deferred pending rules)
DCWP final rules (6 RCNY 5-300 to 5-304) adopted
NY State Comptroller audit finds DCWP enforcement ineffective (complaint-driven); recommends proactive enforcement
Int. 919-2026 (AI oversight office within DCWP) introduced; pending, not enacted as of compilation (unverified on Legistar)

version: Local Law 144 of 2021; DCWP Notice of Adoption of Final Rule (April 2023)
covered_systems: automated employment decision tools: computational processes derived from machine learning, statistical modeling, data analytics or AI that issue simplified output (score, classification, recommendation) used to substantially assist or replace discretionary decision making for employment decisions
exceptions: tools that do not automate, support, substantially assist or replace discretionary decision-making (e.g., junk-mail filters, firewalls, antivirus, calculators, spreadsheets, databases, data sets or other compilations of data)
conditions: Rules define 'substantially assist or replace' as relying solely on simplified output, using it as one of a set of criteria weighted more than any other, or using it to overrule conclusions from other factors including human decision-making
Bias audit must be performed by an independent auditor and be no more than one year old
objective: Reduce discriminatory outcomes from automated hiring and promotion tools by requiring annual independent bias audits, public disclosure of audit summaries, and advance notice to candidates and employees.

related_policies.policy: New York City Human Rights Law
Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964

conflict_rule: Admin. Code § 20-874: the subchapter does not limit any right of a candidate or employee to bring a civil action, or the authority of the NYC Commission on Human Rights to enforce the NYC Human Rights Law (paraphrased).

clauses.original_text: It is unlawful for an employer or employment agency to use an automated employment decision tool to screen a candidate or employee for an employment decision unless (1) the tool has been the subject of a bias audit conducted no more than one year prior to its use, and (2) a summary of the results of the most recent bias audit and the distribution date of the tool are made publicly available on the employer's or agency's website before use.
clauses.requirement: do not use an AEDT without a bias audit less than one year old and a published audit summary
clauses.condition: AEDT used to screen candidates or employees for employment decisions
clauses.purpose: detect and deter disparate impact in hiring and promotion
clauses.affected_asset: candidates' and employees' equal employment opportunity
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: official legislative host was unreachable from the compilation environment, so wording could not be checked against the enacted text. Rules (6 RCNY 5-301) require impact ratios by sex, race/ethnicity and intersectional categories.

clauses.original_text: An employer or employment agency using an AEDT must notify each candidate or employee who resides in the city, no less than ten business days before use, that an AEDT will be used in assessing them, and allow the candidate to request an alternative selection process or accommodation.
clauses.recipient: candidates and employees residing in NYC
clauses.requirement: give notice at least 10 business days before AEDT use and allow request for alternative process or accommodation
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: official legislative host was unreachable from the compilation environment, so wording could not be checked against the enacted text. Law does not itself require providing the alternative process; DCWP rules address notice method.

clauses.original_text: The notice must include the job qualifications and characteristics that the AEDT will use in the assessment of the candidate or employee, provided no less than ten business days before use.
clauses.object: job qualifications and characteristics assessed by the AEDT
clauses.recipient: candidates and employees residing in NYC
clauses.requirement: disclose the qualifications and characteristics the tool assesses
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: official legislative host was unreachable from the compilation environment, so wording could not be checked against the enacted text.

clauses.original_text: If not disclosed on its website, information about the type of data collected for the AEDT, the source of such data and the employer's or agency's data retention policy must be made available upon written request within 30 days.
clauses.object: data type, source and retention policy for AEDT
clauses.requirement: provide data information within 30 days of written request
clauses.condition: information not already posted on website
clauses.exception: disclosure that would violate law or interfere with a law enforcement investigation
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: official legislative host was unreachable from the compilation environment, so wording could not be checked against the enacted text. Exception recalled from enacted text; unverified.

clauses.original_text: A person who violates the subchapter is liable for a civil penalty of not more than $500 for a first violation and each additional violation occurring on the same day, and not less than $500 nor more than $1,500 for each subsequent violation; each day of unlawful use and each failure to give required notice constitutes a separate violation.
clauses.interpretation_notes: Paraphrase, not verbatim: official legislative host was unreachable from the compilation environment, so wording could not be checked against the enacted text. Penalty amounts per compiler's knowledge of statute; DCWP penalty schedule may set lower defaults.
